strings.name: Cai Guo-Qiang
strings.role: Artist · Gunpowder, history and public space
strings.summary: Trained in stage design, Cai develops gunpowder paintings, installations and explosion events. Brief combustion and large collaborations engage local histories, cosmology and public ritual. He developed his practice in Japan and New York, won a Venice Golden Lion in 1999 and designed fireworks for the Beijing Olympics. His work expands painting’s materials and scale; a 2025 Tibet event also led to investigations and ecological restoration responsibilities.
strings.coverageNote: Research cutoff: 2026-11-13. Selected milestones span 1957–2026; this is not a complete catalogue or live news archive.
strings.influence.rationale: Explored cultural exchange and historical memory through gunpowder paintings, explosion projects and public art, extending contemporary art's materials and scale.
strings.facts.fact-01.label: Birthplace
strings.facts.fact-02.label: Education
strings.facts.fact-02.value: Stage design, Shanghai Theatre Academy; graduated in 1985
strings.highlights.highlight-01.title: Combustion as a painting process
strings.highlights.highlight-01.text: Gunpowder, chance and controlled design leave traces on paper and create temporary images in public space.
strings.highlights.highlight-02.title: Large-scale work across places
strings.highlights.highlight-02.text: From Venice to Sky Ladder and Olympic fireworks, his projects connect cultural memory, local settings and collective collaboration.
strings.timeline.event-01.title: Realizes One Page in Porto
strings.timeline.event-01.text: Gunpowder and fireworks created a temporary image over the Douro, commissioned by local literary institutions and co-produced with the city.
strings.timeline.event-02.title: Realizes Radiance of Spring fireworks in France
strings.timeline.event-02.text: Daytime fireworks over the Seine in Vernon marked the Monet centenary, alongside a related exhibition at Mont-Saint-Michel.
strings.timeline.event-03.title: Tibet fireworks investigation is announced
strings.timeline.event-03.text: Xigaze authorities opened proceedings over suspected violations and stated that the studio and sponsor would bear ecological compensation and restoration responsibilities.
strings.timeline.event-04.title: Stages Rising Dragon in Tibet
strings.timeline.event-04.text: The studio staged a commercially sponsored fireworks event in a highland area near Gyantse, prompting controversy over ecological disturbance.
strings.timeline.event-05.title: Realizes Sky Ladder in Quanzhou
strings.timeline.event-05.text: A balloon lifted a ladder-like fireworks structure, realizing an ephemeral ascent into the sky after earlier attempts.
strings.timeline.event-06.title: A retrospective and Beijing Olympics role
strings.timeline.event-06.text: The Guggenheim presented I Want to Believe; he also directed visual effects and fireworks for the Beijing Olympics’ opening and closing ceremonies.
strings.timeline.event-07.title: Wins a Golden Lion in Venice
strings.timeline.event-07.text: Recognition at the 48th Biennale drew international attention to work combining collective production, installation and historical memory.
strings.timeline.event-08.title: Moves from Japan to New York
strings.timeline.event-08.text: After nearly nine years in Japan, he moved to New York and continued gunpowder paintings and site-specific projects within international exhibition networks.
strings.timeline.event-09.title: Completes stage-design studies
strings.timeline.event-09.text: Graduating from Shanghai Theatre Academy, he brought spatial, performative and collaborative experience into painting, installation and fireworks.
strings.timeline.event-10.title: Born in Quanzhou
strings.timeline.event-10.text: Born in Quanzhou, Fujian; local beliefs, crafts and maritime exchange later informed his artistic imagination.
